column1: # Flags declared in BOTH `standalone` and `valued` of one scope, pinned when the overlap became a
# build error (2026-10-15). Nothing is ever added here: a new scope declares the flag once.
# WHAT AN OVERLAP DOES. It behaves as an optional-value flag: the bare spelling takes no value (the
# next word is a positional) and the `=` spelling takes one. A short flag in both lists also refuses
# its glued value (`-ofile`), because the cluster walk reads `o` as a boolean first.
# RESOLVING A ROW. Read the tool's own option table, then move the flag to `optional_valued` (it
# takes `--flag` and `--flag=VALUE`), `valued` alone (it always takes a value) or `standalone` alone
# (it never does), and delete the row. Moving a flag to `valued` approves `--flag VALUE` and `-fVALUE`
# forms that deny today, so it needs the value's path role checked first: on 2026-10-15 a blanket
# move turned 1,139 probe verdicts from deny to allow, `task -d DIR` and `task -t FILE` (which run a
# SHRINKS ONLY. `a_flag_is_never_both_standalone_and_valued_in_one_scope` fails on an overlap that
